// AUTO-GENERATED outer-tiled MX matmul baseline (113x256x256).
void solution(void) {
  // Increase BLK to 4*DIM=64 to fill scratchpad and amortize overhead 16x.
  const int BLK_NEW = 4 * DIM;        // 64
  const int tiles   = BLK_NEW / DIM;  // 4
  const int tiles_K = MATMUL_K / DIM; // 16

  // e8m0 scale: one byte per 32 elements along K => MATMUL_K/32 groups
  // A_s[g][i]: group g, row i within the block (BLK_NEW rows)
  // B_s[g][j]: group g, col j within the block (BLK_NEW cols)
  const int GK        = MATMUL_K / 32;   // 8
  const int A_S_BYTES = GK * BLK_NEW;    // 8 * 64 = 512
  const int B_S_BYTES = GK * BLK_NEW;    // 8 * 64 = 512

  // Scratchpad layout:
  //   A tiles at bottom: a_base=0, uses tiles*tiles_K*DIM = 4*16*16 = 1024 rows
  //   B tiles at top:    b_base = 8192 - 1024 = 7168, uses 1024 rows
  //   Total: 2048 rows <= 8192 — safe, no overlap
  uint32_t b_base = BANK_NUM * BANK_ROWS - tiles * tiles_K * DIM; // 7168
  uint32_t a_base = 0;
  int      SPAD_DEST = 128;

  // Output column count in units of uint64_t words (BF16_PER_WORD BF16 per word)
  const int BLK_OUTC = BLK_NEW / BF16_PER_WORD; // 64/4 = 16

  // Staged scale buffers sized for BLK_NEW-wide blocks
  uint8_t  A_s[GK][BLK_NEW]  __attribute__((aligned(64)));
  uint8_t  B_s[GK][BLK_NEW]  __attribute__((aligned(64)));
  // scale_factors buffer (unused by requantizer logic in spike, but pointer required)
  uint32_t scale_factors[512] __attribute__((aligned(32)));
  memset(scale_factors, 0, sizeof(scale_factors));

  const int NUM_BLOCKS_M = (REAL_M + BLK_NEW - 1) / BLK_NEW; // ceil(113/64) = 2
  const int NUM_BLOCKS_N = (REAL_N + BLK_NEW - 1) / BLK_NEW; // ceil(256/64) = 4

  // Reorder: j0 outer so B tiles can be hoisted; i0 inner sweeps rows.
  for (int j0 = 0; j0 < NUM_BLOCKS_N; j0++) {
    int ncols = REAL_N - j0 * BLK_NEW;
    if (ncols > BLK_NEW) ncols = BLK_NEW;
    if (ncols <= 0) continue;

    // --- Stage B scales ONCE per j0 (weight column-block is fixed across all i0) ---
    for (int g = 0; g < GK; g++)
      memcpy(&B_s[g][0], &B_scales_col[g][j0 * BLK_NEW], BLK_NEW);

    // --- Mvin B tiles ONCE per j0 into the top of the scratchpad ---
    // B is [MATMUL_K][MATMUL_N] in row-major with elem_t=uint8_t (1 byte per element)
    // Row stride for B = MATMUL_N * sizeof(elem_t) = MATMUL_N bytes
    gemmini_config_ld(MATMUL_N * sizeof(elem_t));
    for (int j = 0; j < tiles; j++)
      for (int k = 0; k < tiles_K; k++)
        gemmini_extended_mvin2(
          (void*)(((elem_t*)B_in) + (k * DIM) * MATMUL_N + (j0 * BLK_NEW + j * DIM)),
          b_base + (k * tiles + j) * DIM, DIM, DIM);

    for (int i0 = 0; i0 < NUM_BLOCKS_M; i0++) {
      int mrows = REAL_M - i0 * BLK_NEW;
      if (mrows > BLK_NEW) mrows = BLK_NEW;
      if (mrows <= 0) continue;

      int pad_i = BLK_NEW - mrows;
      int pad_j = BLK_NEW - ncols;

      // --- Stage A scales once per (i0, j0) ---
      for (int g = 0; g < GK; g++)
        memcpy(&A_s[g][0], &A_scales_row[g][i0 * BLK_NEW], BLK_NEW);

      // Step 1: Configure execution (FP8 E4M3 inputs, BF16 output).
      // act_mx_fmt=0 (FP8 E4M3), wgt_mx_fmt=0 (FP8 E4M3), out_mx_fmt=3 (BF16), uselut=0
      gemmini_extended3_config_ex(WEIGHT_STATIONARY, 0, 0, ACC_SCALE_IDENTITY,
                                  1, 1, 0, 0, false, 0, 0, 3, 0);

      // Step 2: Load A and B scales into hardware scale memories.
      // sel=0 → mx_scale_a_mem (activations/A), sel=1 → mx_scale_b_mem (weights/B)
      gemmini_mx_load_scales((uint64_t)A_s, A_S_BYTES, 0);
      gemmini_mx_load_scales((uint64_t)B_s, B_S_BYTES, 1);

      // Step 3: Mvin A tiles for this i0 row-block into scratchpad.
      // A is [MATMUL_M][MATMUL_K] row-major, elem_t=uint8_t
      // Row stride = MATMUL_K * sizeof(elem_t) = MATMUL_K bytes
      gemmini_config_ld(MATMUL_K * sizeof(elem_t));
      for (int i = 0; i < tiles; i++)
        for (int k = 0; k < tiles_K; k++)
          gemmini_extended_mvin(
            (void*)(((elem_t*)A_in) + (i0 * BLK_NEW + i * DIM) * MATMUL_K + k * DIM),
            a_base + (i * tiles_K + k) * DIM, DIM, DIM);

      // Step 4: Configure requantized mvout.
      // i_bound=tiles, j_bound=tiles, k_bound=tiles_K must match loop_ws_spad below.
      // Output stride: BLK_OUTC * sizeof(out_t) bytes per row
      gemmini_config_st(BLK_OUTC * sizeof(out_t));
      gemmini_mxquant_config_mvout((uint64_t)scale_factors,
                                   tiles, tiles, tiles_K, 0, 0, 1);

      // Step 5: Execute fused hardware matmul.
      // mx_loop_spad_marker (funct 24) is re-issued by the macro before every call.
      gemmini_loop_ws_spad(tiles, tiles, tiles_K, pad_i, pad_j, 0,
                           a_base, BANK_NUM * BANK_ROWS, 0, SPAD_DEST,
                           false, false, false, false, false,
                           NO_ACTIVATION, 0, 0, false, 0x38);

      // Step 6: Drain BF16 results from mx_smem to DRAM, row by row.
      // mx_smem word offset for row r = SPAD_DEST*16 + r*BLK_NEW
      // C_hw row pointer offset in uint64_t words = (j0*BLK_NEW)/BF16_PER_WORD
      for (int r = 0; r < mrows; r++)
        gemmini_mx_read_smem(
          &C_hw[i0 * BLK_NEW + r][(j0 * BLK_NEW) / BF16_PER_WORD],
          SPAD_DEST * 16 + r * BLK_NEW, ncols);

      // Step 7: Fence — ensures all mx_read_smem DMA writes are visible to host.
      gemmini_fence();
    }
  }
}
